Cashbook is a manual record-keeping app. It does not connect to any bank, never asks for bank passwords, UPI PINs, card PINs or OTPs, and its reports reflect recorded cash movements only — not a full accrual-based profit and loss account. Consult a qualified professional for tax and statutory matters.
A private, offline-first cashbook for recording income, expenses, cash, bank and wallet balances and transfers.

Built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Data is stored only on this device in an encrypted database (SQLCipher, key protected by the Android Keystore). Amounts are stored as whole paise, so there are no rounding errors. Works on Android 8.0 and newer.

string-array.name: guide
string-array.item: ## Getting started

Cashbook keeps one or more independent cashbooks (for example Personal, Office or Shop). Each cashbook has its own accounts — cash in hand, bank accounts, digital wallets — each with an opening balance and opening date.
## Recording entries

Tap Add in the bottom bar and choose Income, Expense or Transfer. Amount, date, category and account are required; everything else is optional. Use \"Save and add another\" for quick back-to-back entries.
An account is where the money is held; the payment mode is how it moved. A UPI payment from your bank account is recorded against the bank account with mode UPI.
## Transfers

Use Transfer to move money between your own accounts, for example withdrawing cash from the bank. The source account goes down, the destination goes up, and the total does not change. Transfers are never counted as income or expenses.
## Bills and receipts
Attach photos from the camera or gallery, or PDF files, to any entry (up to 10 MB each). Files are stored privately inside the app.
## Finding entries

The Transactions tab supports search, filters (date range, account, type, category, party, payment mode, amount, attachments) and sorting. Filter by a single account and sort Oldest first to see the running balance.
## Balances
Closing balance = opening balance + income − expenses + transfers received − transfers sent. Balances are recalculated automatically whenever an entry is added, edited, deleted or restored.
## Reports
Open Reports, pick a report, choose the period and filters, preview it on screen, then save or share it as a PDF or an editable Excel file. The financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
## Deleting and restoring
Deleted entries go to the recycle bin (Settings › Recycle bin), where you can restore them or delete them permanently. A transfer is always restored as a whole.
## Backups

Settings › Backup & restore creates an encrypted backup file protected by your password. Save it to the phone, an SD card or a cloud drive from the file picker. Keep the password safe — without it the backup cannot be opened.
## Recurring entries and budgets

Settings › Recurring entries schedules rent, salary or subscriptions. Choose whether each one is added automatically or waits on the dashboard for Post / Skip. Open any entry and tap Make recurring to start from it. Settings › Budgets sets monthly limits per expense category; the dashboard shows progress for the current month.
## Invoices, bills and what is owed

Settings › Invoices & bills (or the Receivables & payables card on the dashboard) records sales invoices you raise and purchase bills you receive, with due dates. They don\'t change any balance. When money comes in or goes out, open the invoice and tap Record receipt / Record payment, or apply an entry you already recorded. Status, overdue days and the Outstanding & Ageing report update automatically.
## GST invoices

Fill in Settings › Business profile (name, GSTIN, state, bank/UPI, terms). Then turn on Itemised with GST on an invoice and add lines with HSN/SAC, quantity, rate, discount and GST rate. Supplies within your state are split into CGST + SGST; other states get IGST, based on the place of supply. Save or share the tax invoice as a PDF from the invoice. Reports › GST Summary compares output tax with input tax.
## Credit notes, debit notes and refunds

Open an invoice or bill and tap Credit note (goods returned, discount, overcharge) or Debit note (amount charged short). A credit note starts from the invoice\'s items so you can reduce quantities. Notes change what is owed and the GST summary, never account balances. If a credit note leaves more paid than owed, the invoice shows Refund due — tap Record refund to enter the money returned. Add a logo and signature image in Business profile to print them on invoices and notes.
## Products, services and stock

Settings › Products & services keeps items you bill often with HSN/SAC, unit, sale and purchase rates and GST. On an invoice line tap the box icon (or Add a saved item) to fill it in. For goods, stock is worked out automatically: purchase bills add, sales invoices remove, credit notes for returns reverse them; set an opening stock and a reorder level, and use Stock adjustment for damage or counting differences. Reports › Stock Summary and Item-wise Sales show the details.
## Home-screen widget and alerts

Long-press the home screen › Widgets › Cashbook for quick Income / Expense / Transfer buttons. The balance is shown only if you allow it and the app lock is off. Turn on invoice reminders and budget alerts in Settings › General & financial.
## Automatic backup

In Backup & restore, choose a folder once (phone, SD card or a cloud drive), set a password and turn on Back up automatically. Cashbook saves a backup daily or weekly and keeps only the latest copies.
## Security
Turn on a PIN and, if your phone supports it, fingerprint unlock in Settings › Security. Cashbook never asks for bank passwords, UPI PINs, card PINs or OTPs.

string-array.name: privacy
string-array.item: ## Summary
Cashbook is an offline app. It has no internet permission, contains no advertising or analytics, and does not collect, transmit or sell any personal or financial data.
## Data stored on your device

Your cashbooks, accounts, entries, categories, parties and settings are stored only on this device, in a database encrypted with a key protected by the Android Keystore. Bills and receipts you attach are copied into the app\'s private storage.
## Information we never ask for

Cashbook never asks for bank login passwords, net-banking credentials, UPI PINs, debit or credit card PINs, or OTPs. For bank accounts you may optionally enter only a name and the last four digits of the account number.
## Backups and exports

Backups are encrypted with a password you choose and are saved only to the location you pick in Android\'s file picker (which may be a cloud drive you select). PDF and Excel exports are created only when you ask, and shared only through the Android share menu when you choose to share them.
## Permissions

Notifications: only if you turn on backup reminders, invoice reminders or budget alerts. The optional home-screen widget shows your balance only if you allow it, and never while the app lock is on. Biometrics: only if you turn on fingerprint unlock. Camera photos, gallery images and files are opened through Android\'s system pickers, so Cashbook does not need storage or camera permissions.
## Deleting your data

Delete individual entries or whole cashbooks inside the app, or uninstall the app / clear its data from Android settings to remove everything stored on the device. Backup files you saved elsewhere are under your control.
